We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 5 reactions for target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We have to produce JSON route with 5 reaction steps. Need to find appropriate templates. We have one template (29646) that deprotects TBS? Actually template 29646 is deprotection: converts TBS-protected alcohol to free alcohol (break TBS, form OH). The product is our target? The apply_template gave three possible precursors: each has TBS group attached somewhere. The product is target with free OH groups? The target has multiple OH groups: at position 1 (O attached to chiral carbon), also internal O? Actually target: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. Contains a free OH at start (O attached to chiral carbon). Also an O linking to side chain (O[C@@H]...). That O is an ether linking to side chain; not protected. The TBS groups are not present. So we need to introduce protecting groups in forward direction, but in retrosynthesis we will remove them. So step 1: deprotect TBS to give free OH. So we need a precursor with TBS-protected alcohol(s). The apply_template gave three possibilities. Choose one that seems plausible: e.g., C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO. This has a TBS on the carboxylic acid? Actually O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C attached to the carboxylic acid O? That's a silyl ester of the acid? Not typical. Another: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO. That has TBS on a secondary alcohol. Another: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C (TBS on primary alcohol). Choose one that seems logical: protect primary alcohol (the CH2OH side chain). So precursor: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C. That's target with TBS on the primary alcohol (CH2OTBS). So step 1: deprotect TBS to give target. So retrosynthesis step: target <- precursor (TBS-protected). Template 29646.

Now step 2: need to form that side chain via Still-Gennari (Z-alkene) or HWE (E-alkene). The target has conjugated diene chain with a terminal carboxylic acid. The side chain includes a C=C(CO) double bond (allylic alcohol). Could be formed via HWE from aldehyde and phosphonate. The target also has a terminal carboxylic acid; maybe derived from ester then hydrolyzed later. But we need 5 steps total.

Potential route: 1) deprotect TBS (as above). 2) Oxidize primary alcohol to aldehyde then HWE to install the double bond and carboxylic acid? Actually we have CH2-CH=CH-CH=CH-COOH (a polyene). Could be built via sequential Wittig/HWE. Simpler: start from simpler cyclic core (a tetrahydrofuran?) The core is a cyclohexane with two OH groups and a side chain attached via ether. The core maybe derived from a protected diol.

We can propose steps:

Step 5 (last retrosynthetic) break the ether linking side chain: O-CH2- (the side chain attached via O). So precursor could be phenol? Actually O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C) is an ether linking to side chain. Could be formed by O-alkylation of the cyclic diol with a side chain halide. So step 5: protect the cyclic diol, then alkylate with side chain bromide (or mesylate). So we need a precursor: the cyclic diol (with TBS maybe) and side chain bromide.

But we need 5 steps total. Let's outline:

1) Deprotect TBS on primary alcohol (target from TBS-protected precursor). (Template 29646)

2) Oxidize primary alcohol to aldehyde (DIBAL-H reduction is reverse; forward is oxidation, but we need a template for oxidation? Not given. Could use DIBAL-H reduction in forward direction (reducing ester to aldehyde). In retrosynthesis, we would go from aldehyde to ester via DIBAL-H? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, so reverse is oxidation of aldehyde to ester (not typical). Might be easier: use Still-Gennari to form the double bond and ester from aldehyde and phosphonate. So step 2: apply Still-Gennari (HWE) to convert aldehyde + phosphonate to (Z)-alkene with ester. So precursor: aldehyde (with side chain) and phosphonate. So we need a precursor that is an aldehyde attached to the cyclic core (maybe at the primary position). So after deprotection, we have primary alcohol; we could oxidize to aldehyde then do HWE to get the conjugated diene with ester. But we need 5 steps, so we can combine oxidation and HWE as separate steps.

Step 2: Oxidize primary alcohol to aldehyde (use e.g., PCC). Not in tool list. Might not have template. Could use DIBAL-H reverse: In forward direction DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, so in retrosynthesis we can go from aldehyde to ester (i.e., the aldehyde precursor is derived from ester via DIBAL-H). So step 2: the aldehyde precursor could be derived from an ester precursor via DIBAL-H reduction (forward). So we need a template for DIBAL-H reduction (functional groups broken: carboxylic ester; formed: aldehyde). Search for that.


Search for template where functional_groups_broken includes "carboxylic esters" and formed "aldehydes".
